First, note that if we define the function $g(q,p)$ as
\[g(q,p)=\beta p^TM^{-1}\nabla U(q),\]
then through simple computation we have
\[\mathcal L_A^\dagger\rho_\beta=-\mathcal L_B^\dagger\rho_\beta=g(q,p)\rho_\beta.\]
This is particularly useful as
\[[\mathcal L_A^\dagger,\mathcal L_B^\dagger]\rho_\beta=(\mathcal L_A^\dagger\mathcal L_B^\dagger-\mathcal L_B^\dagger\mathcal L_A^\dagger)\rho_\beta=-(\mathcal L_A^\dagger+\mathcal L_B^\dagger)(g(q,p)\rho_\beta)=(\mathcal L_O^\dagger-\mathcal L_{LD}^\dagger)(g(q,p)\rho_\beta).\]
Now notice that for a function $\psi(q)$ purely of position, we have
\[\mathcal L_{LD}^\dagger(\psi(q)\rho_\beta)=-(p^TM^{-1}\nabla\psi(q))\rho_\beta(q,p),\]
and hence we can compute
\[\mathcal L_O^\dagger(g(q,p)\rho_\beta)=\gamma\rho_\beta(-p\cdot\nabla_pg(q,p)+\beta^{-1}\nabla_p\cdot M\nabla_pg(q,p))=-\gamma g(q,p)\rho_\beta=\gamma\beta\mathcal L_{LD}^\dagger(U(q)\rho_\beta).\]

In summary, we find that
\[f_{1,[ABO]}(q,p)=f_{1,[OAB]}(q,p)=\frac\beta2(\gamma U(q)-p^TM^{-1}\nabla U(q)-c),\tag{7.25a}\]
\[f_{1,[OBA]}(q,p)=f_{1,[BAO]}(q,p)=-\frac\beta2(\gamma U(q)-p^TM^{-1}\nabla U(q)-c),\tag{7.25b}\]
\[f_{1,[AOB]}(q,p)=-\frac\beta2(\gamma U(q)+p^TM^{-1}\nabla U(q)-c),\tag{7.25c}\]
\[f_{1,[BOA]}(q,p)=\frac\beta2(\gamma U(q)+p^TM^{-1}\nabla U(q)-c),\tag{7.25d}\]
where the constant $c$ is chosen to ensure each correction function has average 0, giving $c=\gamma\langle U(q)\rangle$.
